cards.details: Life of Gautama Buddha; formation of the Sangha based on egalitarian principles.
Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali: First major split into Sthaviravadins and Mahasanghikas.
Third Buddhist Council (Ashoka's reign) to purify the Sangha; rise of Vibhajyavada.
Fourth Buddhist Council (Kanishka's reign): Formal split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Second Council split (Sthaviravada vs Mahasanghika) with the Hinayana-Mahayana divide.
Assuming the Sangha was open to everyone; women were only admitted after initial hesitation by the Buddha.
Believing Mahayana is entirely atheistic; it introduced the concept of Bodhisattvas and worship.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Vinaya Pitaka: Rules of discipline.
  • Sangha: Democratically run order.
  • Upasakas: Lay followers.

Sectarian Growth

  • Hinayana: Original doctrine.
  • Mahayana: Liberal/Worship based.
  • Vajrayana: Tantric influences.

Organization and Sects Breakdown

  • The Sangha Structure:
    • Admission was open to all castes, but minors and criminals were excluded.
    • Democratic voting system using wooden sticks (Salakas).
    • Monks (Bhikkhus) and Nuns (Bhikkhunis).
  • Comparison Table:
    SectKey FeatureView on Buddha
    HinayanaStrict/IndividualisticHuman teacher/Guide
    MahayanaUniversal/SalvationDivine/Savior
    VajrayanaTantricEnlightened deity
